text: {"features":[{"evidence":"\"3 years\" versus \"7 years\" of software development","name":"Professional tenure","description":"This captures how much post-degree software engineering experience the letter claims, which signals career stage and likely depth of exposure to production work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Early-career: roughly minimum-qualifying experience is presented, with limited time in industry."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mid-level: several years of experience are presented, suggesting established but not extensive tenure."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Seasoned: long enough tenure is presented to imply broad exposure to production engineering over time."}]},{"evidence":"\"launched 2\" versus \"launched 6 production services\"","name":"Shipping track record","description":"This captures how much repeated production delivery the letter claims, beyond merely having held engineering roles.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Light: the letter mentions few launches or is vague about shipped production work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Moderate: the letter cites multiple production launches, suggesting meaningful delivery experience."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Heavy: the letter shows repeated production launches across several services, implying a strong delivery record."}]},{"evidence":"\"Bachelor's degree\" versus \"Master's degree\" versus \"Doctoral degree\"","name":"Academic level","description":"This captures the highest formal academic credential the applicant explicitly presents.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Bachelor's level: meets the stated minimum educational bar."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Master's level: exceeds the minimum with a relevant advanced degree."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Doctoral level: presents the strongest formal academic credential in the sample."}]},{"evidence":"\"Go and 2 other languages\" versus \"Go and 9 other languages\"","name":"Language breadth","description":"This captures how broadly the letter portrays the applicant's programming experience outside their stated Go background.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Narrow: the letter presents Go plus only a small set of other languages."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Moderate: the letter presents Go plus a meaningful but not especially large range of other languages."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Broad: the letter presents comfort across many other languages, signaling wide technical exposure."}]},{"evidence":"\"I use Python daily\" and \"Python became my workhorse\"","name":"Python depth","description":"This captures how strongly the letter establishes Python as a real production tool rather than a casual secondary skill.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent or weak: Python is omitted or only implied."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Present: Python is mentioned as a language the applicant can use, but depth is unclear."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Strong: Python is described as a regular production tool for services, automation, or analysis."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Central: Python is portrayed as a major part of the applicant's day-to-day engineering across multiple types of work."}]},{"evidence":"\"built and shipped LLM-based features\" and \"built with modern AI directly\"","name":"AI production exposure","description":"This captures whether the letter shows direct experience using AI systems in real shipped software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent: no meaningful AI experience is presented."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Light: AI is mentioned, but the work sounds exploratory or underspecified."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clear: the letter claims shipped production features using modern AI or language models."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strong: AI work is presented as substantial, repeated, and clearly relevant to the role's agent-focused responsibilities."}]},{"evidence":"\"evaluation practices required to operate them\" and \"hardening them against unpredictable inputs\"","name":"AI reliability discipline","description":"This captures whether the letter treats AI as something that must be evaluated, bounded, and made dependable in production.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent: the letter gives no evidence of reliability thinking around AI."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Implied: the letter briefly notes trustworthiness or predictability without showing how it was achieved."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicit: the letter mentions evaluation, hardening, checks, or similar reliability practices for AI systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Operationally mature: the letter frames AI reliability as an engineering discipline with concrete controls and production habits."}]},{"evidence":"\"designed agentic pipelines end to end\" and \"design ownership of agentic tooling\"","name":"Agentic ownership","description":"This captures how much direct ownership the letter claims over building agent-based systems rather than merely using them.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent: no agentic tooling experience is presented."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentioned: agentic systems are referenced, but ownership is unclear or superficial."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Concrete: the letter claims design or implementation of agentic pipelines or tooling."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strong ownership: the letter presents end-to-end architectural responsibility for agent-based systems."}]},{"evidence":"\"bounded, auditable actions\" and \"Go services define their permissions and audit their actions\"","name":"Agent constraint design","description":"This captures whether the letter shows security-minded design for limiting and supervising agent behavior.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent: agent safety or control mechanisms are not discussed."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Basic: the letter mentions boundaries or guardrails in general terms."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Explicit: the letter names concrete controls such as permissions, bounded actions, or auditability."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Rigorous: the letter presents a clear control model with supervision, logging, and constrained autonomy as core design features."}]},{"evidence":"\"threat modeling and code review\" and \"mapping attack surfaces and validating fixes\"","name":"Assessment rigor","description":"This captures how substantive and method-specific the applicant's security assessment experience appears.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent: no real security assessment experience is shown."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Generic: the letter says the applicant has done assessments or reviews, but methods are vague."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Concrete: the letter names specific assessment practices such as threat modeling, code review, or attack-surface analysis."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strong: the letter shows repeated formal assessments tied to findings, remediation, or an explicit attacker-oriented perspective."}]},{"evidence":"\"automates triage of incoming vulnerability reports\" and \"classified, routed, largely self-serve pipeline\"","name":"Triage automation","description":"This captures direct experience automating vulnerability intake, classification, routing, or related response workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent: no vulnerability-handling automation is described."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"General: the letter gestures at security automation but not a specific triage workflow."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Concrete: the letter describes building automation for vulnerability intake, routing, or prioritization."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strong: the letter shows a detailed triage system with functions like classification, deduplication, routing, or clear capacity gains."}]},{"evidence":"\"redesigning an in-memory index\" and \"reworked a matching algorithm\"","name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"This captures how convincingly the letter demonstrates practical strength with data structures and algorithms.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent: no meaningful algorithmic evidence is provided."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claimed: the letter asserts algorithmic strength but gives little concrete proof."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Demonstrated: the letter gives a specific redesign or optimization example grounded in data structures or algorithms."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strongly demonstrated: the letter offers especially substantive or multiple examples that make algorithmic judgment feel central to the applicant's work."}]},{"evidence":"\"occasional patches\" versus \"maintainer of an open-source project\"","name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"This captures how much responsibility the applicant claims in public codebases, from fixing local issues to owning a project.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"None: no open-source contribution is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Patch-level: the letter mentions occasional upstream fixes or contributions."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Active contributor: the letter suggests repeated or meaningful ongoing contribution to open-source tools."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Maintainer: the letter presents ownership of an actively used open-source project, library, or framework."}]},{"evidence":"\"CompTIA Security+\" versus \"OSCP\"","name":"Security credential","description":"This captures the strength of formal security certification the letter cites, if any.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"None: no security credential is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Foundational: the letter cites an entry-level or theory-oriented credential such as Security+."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Hands-on: the letter cites a practical offensive credential such as OSCP."}]},{"evidence":"\"play capture-the-flag competitions\" versus \"near-top finishes\"","name":"Offensive practice","description":"This captures how seriously the letter portrays ongoing adversarial security practice through competitions or similar exercises.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"None: no offensive practice is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Light: the letter mentions occasional participation or general interest."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Regular: the letter presents recurring participation as an active habit."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Serious: the letter shows strong commitment or competitive results, such as top placements."}]},{"evidence":"\"habit-tracking application\" versus \"distributed task queue with exactly-once semantics\"","name":"Side-project ambition","description":"This captures how technically demanding the applicant's personal engineering projects appear.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent or very small: no side project is mentioned, or only a minimal utility appears."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Modest: the letter cites a small end-to-end application or personal tool."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Substantial: the letter cites a technically meaningful systems project beyond a simple app."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"High ambition: the letter cites a demanding distributed or reliability-heavy project with hard design tradeoffs."}]},{"evidence":"\"improvements there are inherited by every team downstream\"","name":"Platform orientation","description":"This captures whether the letter is motivated by central infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Weak: the letter does not emphasize broad platform leverage."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Present: the letter mentions scale or foundational impact in passing."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clear: the letter explicitly prefers foundational work because many teams benefit from it."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strong: the letter repeatedly frames the role as multiplicative, organization-wide leverage and capacity-building."}]},{"evidence":"\"helping busy developer teams do the secure thing by default\"","name":"Developer enablement","description":"This captures whether the letter frames security tooling as a way to help product engineers rather than burden them.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Absent: the letter does not show an internal-user or developer-support mindset."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"General: the letter sounds collaborative, but developer enablement is not a major theme."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clear: the letter explicitly talks about removing friction or helping engineers follow the secure path."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strong: the letter vividly centers secure-by-default tooling, proximity to users, and service to developer teams."}]},{"evidence":"\"security as an engineering discipline rather than a compliance checkbox\"","name":"Security worldview","description":"This captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful philosophy of security as systems engineering rather than mere process or policing.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Thin: the letter shows only generic interest in security."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Emerging: the letter hints at secure development values without a strong philosophy."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clear: the letter explicitly frames security as engineering, design, or infrastructure work."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Strong: the letter offers a well-articulated worldview about secure defaults, systems thinking, and builder-oriented security practice."}]},{"evidence":"\"Having reviewed the posting closely\" and direct references to Go back-end systems, Python AI agents, and vulnerability handling","name":"Posting alignment","description":"This captures how directly the letter maps the applicant's experience to the specific responsibilities and preferred qualifications in the job post.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Generic: the letter could fit many security or backend roles with little adaptation."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Somewhat tailored: the letter mentions Google, security, or scale, but only loosely tracks the posting."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly tailored: the letter addresses several named needs from the posting with matching experience."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Tightly tailored: the letter deliberately maps the applicant to the role's specific mix of Go back ends, Python agents, AI, assessments, and vulnerability response."}]},{"evidence":"frequent misspellings such as \"Engnieer,\" \"taem,\" and \"prdictably\"","name":"Proofreading polish","description":"This captures the mechanical cleanliness of the writing, especially spelling and typographical accuracy.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Poor: frequent distracting errors make the letter feel unpolished."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Fair: noticeable errors recur, though the letter remains readable."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Good: only minor isolated errors appear."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Excellent: the letter is mechanically clean and professionally polished."}]},{"evidence":"fragmented list sentences versus a sustained narrative argument","name":"Letter structure","description":"This captures how well the letter is organized into a coherent, persuasive application rather than a loose inventory of credentials.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Fragmented: the letter reads as disjointed statements or a weakly assembled list."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Functional: the letter is understandable but mostly inventories qualifications without much flow."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Coherent: the letter has a clear progression and makes a readable case for fit."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Persuasive: the letter is tightly structured, purposeful, and rhetorically strong throughout."}]},{"evidence":"specific claims like \"deduplicating findings\" and \"hours of expert attention it returned\"","name":"Evidence specificity","description":"This captures how much the letter backs its claims with concrete examples, technical detail, and visible outcomes.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Abstract: the letter relies mostly on broad claims or aspirations."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Somewhat concrete: the letter includes a few examples, but detail or outcomes remain thin."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Concrete: the letter gives several role-relevant examples with real technical substance."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Highly substantiated: the letter pairs concrete examples with clear ownership, outcomes, or operational consequences."}]}]}
